description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Checkov fixture whose one defective failed check names no location at all. Every value was derived by reading the fixture, the recorded runner metadata and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, and every anchor fact was checked against the pinned tree at 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d -- never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. This is the absent_path class, the one of the six this adapter can produce for which no committed fixture previously existed: it was asserted only from an in-memory record, and a rejection route with no committed fixture is a route nothing has exercised, which AAP 0.9.4 does not permit.
scanner_class_note: Fixed for this tool by AAP 0.5.4's class table and carried unchanged on every row. It does not vary with check_type, with the reporting framework or with record content; trivy is the single tool whose class is decided per record, from the section the record was read from. A rejected record carries no scanner_class at all, because it produces no row.

fixture.top_level_form_note: A single report object -- the form a Checkov artifact takes when one framework reports. The multi-framework array form is covered by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov-alt-shape.json and is not re-covered here: this fixture's subject is the file_line_range field, and testing one thing at a time is what makes a failure attributable.
fixture.summary_note: The report's own summary object, quoted exactly as the base fixture carries it and left untouched by the derivation. It is never used as the record count: the count unit below is the one normalize.reconcile.count_records walks, and the adapter reads summary through report_summaries() only, which returns it verbatim for tool-status.md.
fixture.derivation: Two changes to /results/failed_checks/1 and nothing else in the document. Its three path fields -- file_path, repo_file_path and file_abs_path -- are removed, leaving 25 of its 28 keys; and its file_line_range is restored to the two-element [1, 71] the captured record carries, replacing the base fixture's defective ["20", 20]. Records 0 and 2, the three passed checks, the one skipped check, the one parsing error and the summary are all byte-identical to the base fixture's, verified by canonical-JSON comparison record by record.
fixture.captured_provenance: /results/failed_checks/0 is unmodified captured output: identical to the raw artifact's failed_checks[4] and to the positive fixture's failed_checks[3] on all 28 fields. /results/failed_checks/2 agrees with raw failed_checks[3] on every field it carries and has 27 fields to that record's 28, its captured [1, 47] removed rather than replaced. /results/failed_checks/1 agrees with raw failed_checks[5] on all 25 fields it still carries -- including its restored file_line_range [1, 71] -- and has three fewer, the three path fields the derivation removed. So every value in the defective record is the tool's own output; what makes it defective is what is missing, not anything that was rewritten.
fixture.buckets_are_additions: The passed_checks, skipped_checks and parsing_errors this fixture carries are additions rather than captured content, and stating so keeps the provenance honest. The raw artifact was written under --compact, so all three of its buckets are empty and its summary reports 201 passed against 0 recorded; these three match the positive fixture's, which is where they were carried from. They are what makes the failures-only contract testable at all -- see failures_only.vacuity_note.
fixture.sha256_purpose: The recorded digest is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible. These expectations are re-derived when the fixture changes, never adjusted to keep a test green.
fixture.why_the_line_range_was_restored: So that the fixture carries one fault rather than two. The adapter's classification order puts the path at step 4 and start_line at step 5, so a record missing its path fields AND carrying a defective range would still produce exactly one rejection -- absent_path, because step 4 comes first -- while holding a second defect that nothing ever observes. A fixture whose name states one condition must carry that one condition and no latent others: [1, 71] is the range the captured record really has, so restoring it makes the record sound in every respect except the one under test.
fixture.sibling_fixtures_note: Six other fixtures derive from the same base by altering only that record's file_line_range, and all of them reject it at step 5. This one is the only derivation that reaches step 4, which is why it is also the only one whose recorded rejection identity is the resolver's rather than the adapter's.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- this artifact is not SARIF and routes to the native adapter keyed by the runner that wrote it. It carries no version of "2.1.0" and no runs array, which together are the whole of the SARIF test.
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("checkov", doc) returns tool "checkov", shape "checkov", adapter "checkov", scanner_class "misconfig"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No shape failure is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is a well-formed Checkov report in its object form and routes cleanly; four records inside it are defective, and the adapter rejects those while still emitting the others. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py. This fixture is eligible material for it, being native, but the assertion is that file's and is not restated here.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, of which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py carries the authored copy AAP 0.6.4's import restriction requires. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted, and a test must assert the order rather than the set: a row that carried the twelve keys in some other order would satisfy a set comparison while writing a CSV whose columns did not line up with its header.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS. start_line is one of the five that may be absent, which is what makes this file's central distinction possible: a row may legitimately carry start_line null, so a defective line range that also yielded null would be indistinguishable from a record that honestly states no line.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.worked_example: AAP 0.5.3's first user example, carried in unchanged. Checkov's file_path is relative to the scan target and carries a leading slash, alongside file_abs_path holding the filesystem-absolute path and repo_file_path a root-relative path that also carries a leading slash. The expected path is the leading slash stripped and the remainder treated as root-relative, reconciled against the absolute file_abs_path the same record carries. Every record in this fixture carries all three fields intact, which is deliberate: path resolution is not this fixture's subject, so nothing here may be rejected for its path.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the checkov entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.runner_invocation: one checkov invocation carrying 18 root-relative -d target roots, recorded at runner-metadata.json tools.checkov.invocation_form. This is the fact that makes file_path ambiguous on its own, and therefore the fact that makes an anchor field load-bearing rather than a convenience.
resolution_context.anchor_used: repo_file_path on both rows. The rejected record carries no anchor field and no file_path, so no anchor was available to use and no basis is recorded for it.
resolution_context.anchor_rule: repo_file_path is root-relative and carries a leading slash, so exactly one slash is stripped and the remainder is the row's path. file_abs_path is filesystem-absolute and is relativized to the scan root. The branch is chosen by which field it is, never by whether the value looks absolute -- which is the whole of the worked example, since repo_file_path looks filesystem-absolute while not being it.
resolution_context.file_path_role: corroboration only, on the two rows. Under per_target_directory the slash-stripped file_path is relative to whichever -d root matched, so it corroborates by being a suffix of the anchored path -- and it is, on both rows. The rejected record carries no file_path either, which is what takes it past the unresolvable_path branch and into absent_path.
resolution_context.why_file_path_alone_is_wrong: Stripping the slash off file_path and joining the remainder to the tree root names dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile, a directory that does not exist at the root and which matches no allowlist glob, so every row would silently take in_scope false. Reading the same value as filesystem-absolute is the failure the worked example warns about: it relativizes to a long ../ chain, with nothing crashing. No expected path in this file begins with / or contains a ../ segment.
resolution_context.scan_root_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, spark_src and the checkov entry's resolved_scan_root
resolution_context.root_independence: Both rows below hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given: each path comes from repo_file_path, which is already root-relative and needs no root to resolve. No row carries an absolute path in any field. The rejection is root-independent for a stronger reason: the absent-field check in paths.resolve_checkov_path precedes every branch that consults a base or a root, so no choice of either can change its outcome.
resolution_context.severity_source: the record's own severity field, which is null on every failed check because severities require a licence and BC_API_KEY is deliberately absent. severity.resolve then states the absence rather than assuming a level: severity_native null, severity_norm Info, basis no_vocabulary. No CVSS score is consulted -- a misconfiguration carries none, and AAP 0.5.4's checkov row names severity and nothing else.
resolution_context.start_line_source: file_line_range[0], as an integer. This is the field the whole fixture turns on, and start_line_policy below states every shape it takes here and the outcome each earns.
resolution_context.cwe_and_cve_source: the closed field set guideline, description, short_description, bc_category, benchmarks, details, vulnerability_details. Every one of them is null or an empty array on every record here, so no CWE or CVE token exists to collect and both fields are null on both rows. check_name is deliberately outside that set: it is the row's message, and harvesting an identifier out of a message would put a weakness reference in the dataset that the record never made as a reference.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on both rows. A misconfiguration names a location in a configuration file rather than a package, so no coordinate can be formed -- and that absence is not a rejection: AAP 0.5.4 attaches unformable_package_coordinate to a dependency-oriented record, which this is not.

rejection_boundary.statement: A record that names no location is a rejection. A record whose location resolves outside the twelve authoritative globs is a KEPT row with in_scope false. The two are opposite outcomes and the distinction is the one this fixture sits beside: absence of a path is a defect, while a path outside scope is an ordinary answer.
rejection_boundary.why_the_defective_record_can_only_be_a_r: Because path is not one of the five fields AAP 0.8.2 permits to be absent. A row with a null path would assert that the pipeline understood a record which named nothing, and emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS would refuse it in any case. AAP 0.5.4's rule is to reject rather than infer where a record cannot be attributed with certainty, and a record with no location cannot be attributed at all.

not_a_rejection.case: a path resolving outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: Out of scope means kept and marked, never rejected. Checkov legitimately reaches such coordinates, since its reach is shaped by its eighteen -d roots while in_scope is the allowlist's answer and not the runner's. Every path in this fixture is inside the globs, so rows_out_of_scope is 0.

not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with start_line null
not_a_rejection.evidence: /results/failed_checks/2 is exactly this, and it is row index 1 below. Absence IS permitted for start_line, which is the contrast that makes path's non-optionality worth stating: one field's absence is a row and the other's is a rejection, in the same document.

not_a_rejection.case: a record carrying file_path but no anchor field
not_a_rejection.expected: a counted rejection under unresolvable_path, a different class
not_a_rejection.evidence: A location IS named, so the record is not absent-path; it cannot be placed against one of eighteen targets, which is the other class. Owned by reject-checkov-unresolvable-path.json.

not_a_rejection.expected: no row and no rejection at all
not_a_rejection.evidence: The bucket decides, never the check_id: this fixture's skipped CKV_DOCKER_9 shares its check_id with no surviving failed check here but does share its file with row index 1. Neither counted nor emitted, per failures_only below.

not_a_rejection.case: a parsing error the tool reported
not_a_rejection.expected: status evidence for tool-status.md, neither a row nor a rejection
not_a_rejection.evidence: Counting one as a rejection would make rejections 2 while the independent traversal still returned 3, breaking the identity for something that was never a finding.

rejection_boundary.no_guessed_path: Repeated from path_policy because it is the assertion a reader is most likely to want twice: neither the record's own resource field nor the neighbouring record's location may be read as this record's path, and no expected row carries either.

failures_only.count_unit: one element of results.failed_checks[], the union across every report object in either top-level shape
failures_only.passed_checks_note: Neither counted nor emitted, and no passed check's identity may appear anywhere in the rows array. All three pass on resource-managers/kubernetes/docker/src/main/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile: line 71 of that file is USER ${spark_uid} -- the last instruction, and not root -- which is why CKV_DOCKER_3 and CKV_DOCKER_8 pass, and its single FROM at line 20 carries an explicit tag, which is why CKV_DOCKER_7 passes. CKV_DOCKER_7 matters more here than a passed check usually would: it is the record carrying the genuine [20, 20] range, so an adapter that read the passed bucket would emit a row whose start_line 20 looked like a successful coercion of the defective values rather than what it was. They are observable only through the passed_checks_observed counter, which is what makes produced-no-row an observation rather than a claim.
failures_only.skipped_checks_note: Neither counted nor emitted, exactly as passed checks are not. The one entry is CKV_DOCKER_9 on bindings/R/Dockerfile at file_line_range [34, 37] carrying suppress_comment "baseline-skipped", and it must produce no row even though the identical check_id on another file does -- the bucket decides that, never the check_id. It carries a second load here: it names the SAME file as /results/failed_checks/2, whose file_line_range is absent, and it holds a perfectly usable [34, 37]. That usable range must not be borrowed to supply the companion row's missing line. Attribution is per record, and taking a field from a neighbouring record is exactly the inference AAP 0.1.3 forbids -- and here it would also destroy the fixture's boundary, by turning the legitimate absence into a line.
failures_only.parsing_errors_note: Status evidence for oss-scan-results/tool-status.md, carried verbatim, and neither a finding nor a rejection. The distinction is sharper in this fixture than in most: the parsing-error entry is an ABSOLUTE PATH, and the record this fixture rejects is rejected for having no path at all -- so an implementation that reached into the parsing-errors array for a location would produce a row naming a shell script the record never mentioned. A rejection describes a failed check this adapter could not turn into a row; a parsing error is the tool's report about a file it never turned into a check, and it is not one of the counted failed checks. Counting it would make rejections 2 while the independent traversal still returned 3.
failures_only.vacuity_note: The three zero expectations above are why this fixture carries non-empty passed_checks, skipped_checks and parsing_errors at all. Against an artifact whose buckets were empty -- which is what the raw artifact's --compact output is -- the failures-only contract would be satisfied by an adapter that read every bucket, and the assertion would prove nothing.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of results.failed_checks[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("checkov", doc), whose traversal reduces both top-level shapes to a sequence of report objects and sums the length of each results.failed_checks array, building no row, resolving no path and reading no file_line_range. It reads reconcile.CHECKOV_COUNTED_SECTION and nothing else, so passed_checks, skipped_checks and parsing_errors contribute zero by construction. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing -- and on this fixture in particular it is the only count that cannot be distorted by the field under test, since it never looks at file_line_range at all.
counts.rejection_class_count_note: One class, because this fixture carries one defect: one record naming no location, among two sound ones. The five other rejection classes this adapter can produce are owned by separately named fixtures, so a test comparing rejections_by_class here is comparing an attributable measurement rather than a mixture.
counts.reconciliation_status_authority: normalize.reconcile, STATUS_PASS = "pass". Its STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE and the verdict reconcile.NOT_APPLICABLE_ABSENT are for a tool that wrote no artifact and are not in play here: this artifact exists and carries records.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.note: Named here rather than restated with their values. The counters block below is the single measurement, and a number carried twice inside one document is a number that can drift; counters_note gives the reason each of the four is zero.

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned as partial where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and the one rejected record is counted under its class, with its reason retained.
counts.row_count_note: 2 is not len(results.failed_checks): it is that length minus the one rejected record. Three passed checks, one skipped check and one parsing error sit in the same document, and any one of them leaking in would make this 3, 4, 5 or 6, while the rejected record given a guessed path would make it 3 with the identity still balancing -- which is why the rejections array below is asserted by class, detail and identity rather than by count alone.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): nineteen authored keys, one path_kind_* per member of normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS and one severity_basis_* per member of normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES -- twenty-eight in all, every one an int.
counters_note: Four values a reader must not 'correct'. First, start_line_absent is 1 rather than 2, and the second is not the rejected record: only /results/failed_checks/2 is a row whose line is legitimately absent. The rejected record carries a perfectly sound file_line_range [1, 71] and never reaches step 5 at all, because step 4 rejected it -- so it contributes to no start_line counter in either direction. Second, every severity, path_kind and scope counter is 2 rather than 3: those are incremented only while a row is being built, which is after step 5, so a record rejected at step 4 contributes to none of them. path_kind_tree_file 2 is the sharpest of these -- the rejected record has no path kind because it has no path. Third, path_corroboration_recorded is 0: the two rows carry three agreeing path fields each, and the rejected record carries none at all, so there was nothing anywhere in this document to disagree. Fourth, the four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool are all 0: caller_file_path is null on every record, no record carries a CWE or CVE identifier in the closed source field set, and both emitted paths name a file inside the scanned tree.
counters_root_note: Given some other absolute scan root, no counter above changes and no row changes. Both rows take their path from repo_file_path, which needs no root; the rejection is decided from file_line_range, which no root touches. The positive sibling's path_corroboration_recorded is root-dependent because its records carry two resolvable anchors that would disagree under a different root; here the anchors agree, so even that dependency is absent.

recorded_divergences.subject: the emitted path's relationship to file_path
recorded_divergences.brief_states: the leading-slash convention is preserved -- a row's path is its record's file_path minus the leading slash
recorded_divergences.fixture_yields: each row's path is the anchored path -- repo_file_path minus exactly one leading slash -- of which the stripped file_path is a proper suffix
recorded_divergences.resolution: The authored contract governs, and it is the same contract the already-committed positive and unresolvable-path siblings record. Under the recorded path_base.kind per_target_directory the stripped file_path is relative to whichever of 18 -d roots matched, so it cannot be the row's path: dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile names no location at the root. AAP 0.5.4's generic checkov row -- path from file_path with its leading slash stripped, reconciled against file_abs_path -- describes the single-target shape; runner-metadata.json records the shape this provisioning actually invoked, and the AAP requires that metadata be read as input rather than assumed. Both readings are stated here so the difference is visible. The leading-slash convention itself is preserved either way: exactly one slash is stripped, from whichever field is the anchor.
recorded_divergences.assertion_that_holds_instead: For every row: the path carries no leading slash and no ../ segment, the stripped file_path is a suffix of it, and the relativized file_abs_path equals it exactly. That is strictly stronger than the brief's equality, and it is what row_derivations records per row under path_cross_check and file_path_is_suffix_of_anchored_path.

corroboration.note: Only one of the two rows is captured output that already appears elsewhere, so only one can be corroborated rather than merely asserted. Row 0 here is the positive sibling's row 3 and all twelve field comparisons agree; the committed dataset carries the same finding, CKV_DOCKER_9 at start_line 36 on resource-managers/kubernetes/docker/src/main/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile. Row 1 has no counterpart to corroborate against and is asserted from the fixture and the contracts alone: its captured origin appears in both of those sources with start_line 1 rather than null, because the captured record carries file_line_range [1, 47] and the base fixture's derivation removes it. That difference is the derivation holding, not a discrepancy. Recorded after the fact rather than as the source of these values: each was derived from the fixture and the authored contracts, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply. The rejected record has no counterpart at all -- a captured Checkov failed check always names its file, so a record naming none exists only as this fixture's derivation, appears in no captured artifact, and contributes no dataset row.
corroboration.dataset_rows_not_expected_here: The committed dataset carries six checkov rows; four of them come from records this fixture does not carry at all, and one from a record whose line range this derivation removed, so their absence from these rows is the fixture's construction holding rather than a discrepancy.

rows.message: Ensure that HEALTHCHECK instructions have been added to container images

row_derivations.role_in_this_fixture: The control. It is one of two records the derivation left untouched, so it proves the adapter still resolves an ordinary path from an ordinary anchor while the record beside it is being rejected for having none. It sits FIRST, before the defect, which is what makes row index 1 the load-bearing one: a run that died on the defect at check index 1 would still produce this row.
row_derivations.bc_check_id_note: null here, and never a fallback for check_id in any case: AAP 0.5.4 names check_id as the source of rule_id.
row_derivations.message_note: check_name and nothing else. The record's check_result.results_configuration quotes a thirteen-line RUN instruction including apt invocations and a pam.d redirection, and none of that text reaches any field of this row.
row_derivations.severity_native_note: null in the record, because severities require a licence and BC_API_KEY is absent; the absence is stated rather than a level assumed
row_derivations.path_transform: exactly one leading slash stripped; the remainder is already root-relative
row_derivations.start_line_outcome: the first element is the integer 36, at or above 1, so it is emitted unchanged
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: every field in the closed identifier source set is null or an empty array on this record, so no CWE token exists to collect
row_derivations.glob_match_note: the mid-path ** absorbs the single segment docker, and the trailing ** absorbs dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile -- zero-or-more-directories semantics, which fnmatch and PurePath.match do not provide
row_derivations.pin_evidence: Verified at the pinned commit: the file is exactly 71 lines, line 36 is the RUN set -ex && \ instruction that opens the block whose captured range is [36, 48], and line 48 is inside the file. The instruction really does invoke apt-get update and apt install, so CKV_DOCKER_9 genuinely fails and this row is real tool output rather than a fixture artefact. start_line 36 is within the file, and no start_line anywhere in this file exceeds 71.

row_derivations.derivation: The captured record's file_line_range -- the two-element [1, 47] -- was REMOVED rather than replaced, so this record carries 27 fields to the captured record's 28 and every one of the 27 is the tool's own output. Removal rather than nulling is deliberate: it exercises the absent-field route through _start_line, which is a different early return from the explicitly-null-first-element route.
row_derivations.role_in_this_fixture: The continuation proof, and the contrast that makes path's non-optionality legible. It is a valid failed check whose file_line_range is absent and whose expected row carries start_line null -- so one field's absence is a row while the other's, one record earlier, is a rejection. It is positioned LAST, after the defect, so its presence in the output is what proves the adapter carried on past a record it could not place.
row_derivations.bc_check_id_note: null here, and never a fallback for check_id in any case: AAP 0.5.4 names check_id as the source of rule_id.
row_derivations.severity_native_note: null in the record, because severities require a licence and BC_API_KEY is absent; the absence is stated rather than a level assumed
row_derivations.path_transform: exactly one leading slash stripped; the remainder is already root-relative
row_derivations.start_line_outcome: the field is absent from the record, so _start_line returns None with no rejection and the row carries JSON null -- the absence convention, and one of the five fields AAP 0.8.2 permits it for
row_derivations.not_a_rejection: Stated explicitly because it is the assertion most easily lost. This record must be a ROW, not a rejection. Its path resolves cleanly from repo_file_path and only its line information is absent, which is permitted -- and an implementation that treated any absent field as a defect would reject both records and report two rejections with one row, still balancing the identity at 3.
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: every field in the closed identifier source set is null or an empty array on this record, so no CWE token exists to collect
row_derivations.glob_match_note: the mid-path ** absorbs docker and the trailing ** absorbs dockerfiles/spark/bindings/R/Dockerfile -- three segments after src/main, which a single-* matcher would refuse
row_derivations.pin_evidence: Verified at the pinned commit: the file is exactly 47 lines and contains zero HEALTHCHECK instructions, so CKV_DOCKER_2 genuinely fails and this row is real tool output. The captured range this derivation removed was [1, 47], a whole-file range spanning the file exactly -- which is why removing it leaves a record that is still perfectly meaningful without a line.
row_derivations.position_note: This record was at /results/failed_checks/5 before the fixture was reduced. Its 27 fields are byte-for-byte the same; only its index moved, from 5 to 2, as three records ahead of it were relocated to their own fixtures.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer names the record. Unlike this adapter's own step-5 rejections, the report_index / check_index / check_type triple does NOT appear in the recorded identity below: this rejection is built by paths.resolve_checkov_path and returned to the adapter as-is, so its identity is the resolver's -- the record's own fields -- rather than the adapter's traversal coordinates. The triple is carried here because it is what a human opens the fixture with.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the paths.REJECT_ABSENT_PATH constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten. Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, so the class name is what carries the assertion.
rejections.reject_class_description: the record carries no path field, or carries one that is empty
rejections.reject_class_description_source: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, REJECT_CLASS_DESCRIPTIONS. A test should read the description from that mapping rather than from this restatement of it. Note that the canonical description names the two shapes this class covers -- no path field, or a path field that is empty -- and this fixture carries the first: three fields absent rather than one present and blank. The blank-value shape is reached through the same branch of paths.resolve_recorded_path for the tools whose path is a single scalar field, and for checkov it is a non-blank string test inside resolve_checkov_path's anchor loop.
rejections.raised_by: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, resolve_checkov_path -- not by the adapter. The adapter returns the resolver's Rejection unchanged, deliberately: paths.py has already named the class, written the sub-reason and built the identity, and rewording any of the three would lose it.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Steps 1 to 3 pass on this record: it is a JSON object, it carries check_id CKV_DOCKER_2, and it carries a non-empty check_name. Step 5 is never reached, which is why its sound file_line_range [1, 71] is never read.
rejections.fields_consulted_note: The two recorded anchor fields, in the order the runner metadata records them, followed by file_path. All three are absent from this record, which is the whole of the condition. The list is composed by the resolver from the metadata rather than hardcoded, so it is also what the detail below names.

rejections.expected_detail_must_not_contain_note: The first would mean the record was classified at step 5 rather than step 4; the second is the unresolvable_path detail's own phrase and would mean the two classes had been confused; the third belongs to the container-shape branch.
rejections.record_identity_note: One key, and the count is the assertion. resolve_checkov_path builds its identity from check_id, file_path and repo_file_path, keeping only those the record carries a non-null value for -- and this record carries only the first. So the identity is not merely small, it is exactly as large as the record permits: an identity carrying a path field here would mean the resolver had found a location it then reported as absent. Contrast the six sibling fixtures, whose step-5 rejections carry the adapter's four traversal keys instead.
rejections.identity_is_enough_to_find_the_record: check_id CKV_DOCKER_2 appears twice among this fixture's three failed checks, so the identity alone does not single the record out. That is a property of the resolver's identity contract rather than a defect in the fixture, and it is why the pointer and the report_index / check_index pair are recorded above: a reader locating the record uses those, while a test comparing identities uses the resolver's.
rejections.why_not_a_row: A row would have to state a path. There is nothing to state: no field of the record names a location, so any value emitted would be one this pipeline invented. Emitting null is not available either -- path is not one of the five fields absence is permitted for, and emit.py would refuse the row.
rejections.why_not_unresolvable_path: That class is for a record that DOES name a location which cannot be placed -- a file_path with no anchor field, under a recorded path_base.kind of per_target_directory. This record names nothing at all, so there is no location to fail to place. The presence or absence of file_path is what separates the two, and it is tested before either base branch is consulted.
rejections.why_not_malformed_record: The record IS a JSON object with every other field the adapter reads -- an intact check_id, an intact check_name, a sound two-element file_line_range. Its shape is fine; what is missing is a location, which has its own class.
rejections.contributes_no_counter: It contributes to no counter at all, in either direction. Every severity, path_kind and scope counter is incremented only while a row is being built, which is after step 5; start_line_absent likewise. multi_location_records is the one counter taken before the path step, and caller_file_path is null on this record, so even that stays 0. The record is visible in the output solely as this rejection and in the arithmetic 3 == 2 + 1.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: The rejected record is never fed to the severity tally, so no native literal from it reaches severity-map.md. That document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains, and this record contributes none. Its severity is null in any case, which is exactly what makes the omission easy to miss and worth stating.

scope_of_this_file.records_only_this_tool: These are checkov's rows and rejections and nothing else. Trivy also reports misconfigurations on the same Dockerfiles, and that produces trivy's own rows in trivy's own expected file: no comparison, no deduplication, no ranking and no cross-tool interpretation is made here, and nothing in this file characterises a finding as real, important or a false positive. Two tools reporting the same location produce two rows and no comment. The sibling reject-trivy-non-integer-start-line fixture asserts the same class on the same kind of value for that tool, and the two are not compared either -- each states its own adapter's contract.
scope_of_this_file.no_deduplication: CKV_DOCKER_9 appears once among the failed checks and CKV_DOCKER_2 twice, and CKV_DOCKER_9 appears again in the skipped bucket. Nothing here collapses them: the two failed checks that survive produce two rows, and the one that does not survive produces one separately counted rejection -- not a row merged into its namesake.
scope_of_this_file.no_secret_value: No field carries a secret or any content from check_result.results_configuration. message is check_name and nothing else, so the multi-line shell text those records quote -- including the apt invocations, the pip invocation and the pam.d redirection -- reaches no row and no rejection detail. The absolute paths that appear are quoted evidence about the fixture, never emitted data, and the only literal values quoted from the artifact are the defective line ranges themselves. This tree is committed to git.
scope_of_this_file.no_inference: A record whose location cannot be established is a counted rejection, never a path picked from the record's own resource field, from an adjacent record, from the parsing-errors array, or from the scan root. This file is where that rule is exercised for checkov's absent_path class, and it is why the file carries one rejection and two rows rather than three rows with a plausible location in one of them.
scope_of_this_file.no_judgement_of_the_findings: That the three anchor Dockerfiles carry no HEALTHCHECK and do invoke apt is recorded as the reason CKV_DOCKER_2 and CKV_DOCKER_9 fire, and therefore as evidence the surviving rows are real tool output. It is not a claim that either finding matters, and no remediation is suggested anywhere.
scope_of_this_file.not_a_run_transcript: Every value in this file was derived by reading the fixture, the pinned tree and the authored contracts, and the corroboration run came afterwards and agreed. The direction is fixed: where this file and the adapter disagree, the disagreement is the finding to diagnose, and no adapter under harness/lib/normalize/ is edited to make an assertion in this corpus pass.

path_policy.statement: path is not an optional field. AAP 0.5.4 permits absence for exactly five fields -- severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate -- and path is not among them, so a record that names no location cannot become a row with a null path. It is rejected and counted under absent_path.
path_policy.absence_permitted_fields_do_not_include_: Restated because the mistake is easy to make in the other direction: this corpus's start-line fixtures turn on the fact that an ABSENT start_line is a legitimate row, so a reader could reasonably expect an absent path to be one too. It is not. emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS carries path, and emit.py refuses a row without one, which is why the adapter must reject rather than emit.
path_policy.adapter_contract: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, resolve_checkov_path. The anchor fields come from the recorded runner metadata -- repo_file_path then file_abs_path -- and each is tried in turn where the record carries a non-blank string for it. Where no anchor matched AND the record carries no usable file_path either, the record names no location and the class is absent_path. Where no anchor matched but a file_path IS present, the outcome depends on the recorded path_base.kind: under scan_root the slash-stripped file_path really is root-relative and resolves, and under per_target_directory it cannot be placed and the class is unresolvable_path.

class_boundary.absent_path: the record carries NONE of repo_file_path, file_abs_path and file_path, so there is no location to resolve. This fixture.
class_boundary.unresolvable_path: the record carries file_path and no anchor field, under a recorded path_base.kind of per_target_directory: a location IS named, and there is no way to know which of the runner's eighteen -d targets it is relative to. Owned by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/reject-checkov-unresolvable-path.json.
class_boundary.why_the_two_are_separate_classes: One says the producer named nothing; the other says the producer named something this pipeline cannot place. Collapsing them would make tool-status.md unable to tell a defective artifact from a configuration this normalizer cannot resolve, which are different problems with different owners. paths.REJECT_CLASS_DESCRIPTIONS keeps them apart and so does this fixture set.
class_boundary.the_check_order_decides: In resolve_checkov_path the corroborator -- the slash-stripped file_path -- is computed before the anchor loop, and the absent_path branch is the one taken when that corroborator is None and no anchor matched. So the presence or absence of file_path is what separates the two classes, and it is tested before either base branch is consulted. That ordering is why this rejection is independent of the recorded path_base.kind while the unresolvable_path one is not.

path_policy.the_detail_names_the_fields_it_looked_fo: The diagnostic lists the recorded anchor fields followed by file_path, in that order, so a reader of tool-status.md can see exactly which fields were consulted rather than having to know the resolver's contract. It is composed from the anchors the metadata supplied, which means a provisioning recording different anchor fields would produce a different detail -- and this expected file records the detail for the anchor pair this run's metadata actually carries, [repo_file_path, file_abs_path].
path_policy.no_guessed_path: The rejected record is not given a path, not even a plausible one, and nothing in this file supplies one for it. Two plausible guesses are available and both are refused: the record's own resource field spells /dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile. -- the file_path with a trailing dot -- and the record beside it names resource-managers/kubernetes/docker/src/main/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile outright. Reading either would be the inference AAP 0.1.3 forbids: resource is not a path field, and a neighbouring record's location is not this record's.
path_policy.the_resource_field_is_not_a_path_field: Worth stating on its own, because this record still carries resource "/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile." and check_class "checkov.dockerfile.checks.HealthcheckExists" after the derivation, and the first of those looks like a path. It is Checkov's own resource identifier -- the file_path with the resource name appended after a dot -- and the closed set of fields resolve_checkov_path reads is the two recorded anchors plus file_path and nothing else. Harvesting a location out of resource would put a path in the dataset the record never stated as one, and the trailing dot shows why: it is not a filename.
path_policy.start_line_is_not_this_fixture_s_subject: The rejected record's file_line_range is the sound captured [1, 71] and is never read, because step 4 rejects before step 5 runs. Recorded so a reader does not look for a line-range defect here: this fixture's whole subject is the path, and the six fixtures that own the line-range routes are named under behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture.

counters_shared_with_the_base_fixture: All 28 values above are identical to oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/reject-checkov-non-integer-start-line.rows.json's, and to those of the six other fixtures derived from the same base. It is worth stating because a reader comparing two of these expected files would otherwise read the identical counters as a copy-paste error.
